children: , the diabetes and obesity-drug powerhouse, traded at $1,154.24 Thursday as Mounjaro secured a concrete African growth target. Distributor Aspen Pharmacare expects regional sales to break 2 billion rand, or roughly $124 million, in the year ending June 2027.

South Africa is already moving fast. The country's GLP-1 market nearly doubled to 2.8 billion rand over the past year, while Mounjaro's share rocketed from 15% to 53%. Strong demand is doing the heavy lifting today. Pending registrations in Kenya and Nigeria could widen Lilly's runway tomorrow.

Lilly generated $9.94 billion from Mounjaro last quarter, so Aspen's entire annual target equals only about 1.25% of one global quarter. Africa will not move Lilly's numbers yet. But distribution, approvals and physician adoption could lock in an early lead before the regional market gets serious. Meanwhile, the stock sits 24.44% below its GF Value estimate of roughly $1,530a valuation gap investors cannot casually ignore.

title: Lilly's African Mounjaro Push Starts at 1.25% of Quarterly Sales
